The deadweight loss is the integral of the difference between demand price and supply price from the after-tax quantity \(Q_t\) to the equilibrium quantity \(Q_0\).  
The difference \(D(Q) = \text{demand price} - \text{supply price}\) is piecewise linear.  
\(Q_t\) satisfies \(D(Q_t) = 826\). Using the first segment (\(0 \le Q \le 10\)):  
\(D(Q) = 827 - \frac{3}{5}Q\). Setting \(827 - \frac{3}{5}Q = 826\) gives \(Q_t = \frac{5}{3}\).  
\(Q_0\) satisfies \(D(Q_0) = 0\). Using the segment \(1190 \le Q \le 1200\):  
\(D(Q) = 8 - \frac{9}{10}(Q-1190)\). Setting \(D(Q)=0\) gives \(Q_0 = 1190 + \frac{80}{9} = \frac{10790}{9}\).  

The area under \(D(Q)\) from \(0\) to \(Q_0\) is the sum of trapezoidal areas from \(0\) to \(1190\) plus the triangular area from \(1190\) to \(Q_0\).  
The sum from \(0\) to \(1190\) is \(495185\) (computed from the data points).  
The triangle from \(1190\) to \(Q_0\) has area \(\frac{320}{9}\).  
Thus \(\int_0^{Q_0} D(Q)\,dQ = 495185 + \frac{320}{9} = \frac{4456985}{9}\).  

The area from \(0\) to \(Q_t\) is \(\int_0^{5/3} \left(827 - \frac{3}{5}Q\right)dQ = \frac{2755}{2}\).  

Hence the deadweight loss is  
\[
\int_{Q_t}^{Q_0} D(Q)\,dQ = \frac{4456985}{9} - \frac{2755}{2} = \frac{8889175}{18}.
\]  
This fraction is already in lowest terms.

ANSWER: 8889175/18
